description: Alien Touch Gravity— a bunch of curious minds trying to solve space problems with code, creativity and a little chaos! We’ve got Python, C++, AI, cybersecurity, and big ideas. No spaceship yet, but we’re working on it. Join us and let’s build something awesome for NASA!
summary:
"The Moons Midnight Mystery" is a 26-page illustrated children's storybook. Maya, a girl finds a mysterious signal in NASAs online space archives at 12:07 a.m. It carries her to the Moon, where she meets four machines: Surveyor 3 the Apollo 11 laser retroreflector and the Apollo 12 and Apollo 15 science experiment packages (ALSEP). Each machine tells its story in a friendly voice. Along the way Maya earns three Memory Keys (Curiosity, Patience and Knowledge) and uncovers a secret, the knowledge these missions left behind.

The project turns NASA mission history into a story young readers can enjoy. Facts such as Surveyor 3s bounce, its 6,326 pictures, laser distance measurement and moonquake detection are woven into the narrative.

This matters because older missions are often forgotten once they end. The book shows that their data and discoveries still shape what we know and it encourages children to stay curious, about space. Its message is that the end of a mission is not the end of a discovery.
details:
The Moon's Midnight Mystery is a 26-page illustrated digital storybook for children. It has a prologue, five chapters and an epilogue. Maya, a curious girl, receives a mysterious signal while browsing NASA's online space archives. It carries her to the Moon, where she meets four machines in turn:

  • Surveyor 3
  • the Apollo 11 laser retroreflector
  • the Apollo 12 science experiment team (ALSEP)
  • the Apollo 15 science experiment team (ALSEP)

Each machine tells its own story and teaches a real fact. Examples are Surveyor 3's two bounces on landing and its 6,326 pictures, laser measurement of the Earth–Moon distance, and moonquakes. Readers collect three Memory Keys (Curiosity, Patience and Knowledge). They then reach the "fifth secret": the knowledge these missions left behind.

Benefits

  • It makes real NASA mission history easy for young readers to follow.
  • It gives forgotten, decades-old missions a friendly voice.
  • It models curiosity, patience and asking questions.
  • Its mystery structure and keys keep readers engaged, and the book can be read on any screen.

Intended impact

We want children to see that a space mission's work does not end when its machines go silent. The data and discoveries keep shaping what we know. We hope it inspires young readers to explore space science and become explorers themselves.

Tools and technology

  • Storybook writing and layout [ Canva / Google Docs / Word doc]
  • Illustrations: [ AI-assisted : Claude]
  • Final format: PDF digital storybook
  • Research sources: [NASA Surveyor and Apollo mission pages]
  • Presentation deck: built with Claude

Creativity

  • The machines are characters with personalities, such as a proud little robot that "bounced twice".
  • A midnight mystery frame (12:07 a.m., "Unknown access detected") draws readers in.
  • Memory Keys give a game-like sense of progress.
  • The twist is that the "fifth machine" is not a machine at all. It is knowledge.

Factors we considered

  • Accuracy: mission details such as dates, astronauts and instrument purposes are based on NASA records
  • Audience: simple language, short lines and a friendly tone for young readers.
  • Visual design: a glowing space palette with consistent characters across scenes.
  • Emotional arc: machines that seem forgotten turn out to have a lasting legacy.
  • Accessibility: a digital format anyone can open, with clear text beside each illustration.
